fiscal_year_end: 1 August (fiscal year ending date labels the FY, e.g. FY2025 = year ended 1 Aug 2025)
horizon_rationale: Base-case owner-FCF margin is still rising at Year 5 (8.26%) vs Year 10 (8.86%) — margin has not matured by Year 5 (working-capital drag from strong early growth suppresses Y1 margin to 6.50%, well below the FY2025 actual of 8.64%). Extended to 10 years so the terminal year capitalizes a matured margin rather than one still climbing.

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2017-FY2025 cash flow reconciliation; SBC negligible ($0.0-0.2m/yr) — no material LTI expense line, treasury share movements only
inputs.ifrs16_note: IFRS 16 adopted FY2020. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) excludes rent (now in financing as lease principal repayments), inflating reported FCF by the lease principal amount vs a pre-IFRS16 basis. Owner FCF deducts actual lease principal repayments (sourced per-year from cash flow statements in Extracted/) to restore a rent-inclusive, economically comparable FCF. Lease liabilities (~$76.6m FY2025) are excluded from net-debt (operating lease obligations, not financial debt), consistent with treating their cash service cost (principal + interest) as an operating cash outflow in owner FCF instead.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of equity_5yr_cagr (5.1%) and revenue/NPAT trend (~9-11%), weighted toward the conservative equity anchor but adjusted up given HLG's ~85% payout ratio structurally suppresses equity CAGR relative to true earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (5.1%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (10.3%). This is NOT a quality red flag: HLG pays out ~80-90% of earnings as dividends (FY2025 DPS $0.51 / EPS $0.66), so retained earnings — and hence book value growth — mechanically lag revenue/earnings growth. Revenue and NPAT CAGRs are the more meaningful growth signals for this income-oriented compounder; equity CAGR understates growth because most profit leaves the balance sheet as dividends rather than being retained.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF CAGRs are noisy and not used as the primary growth anchor: the 5yr figure (-0.8%) is distorted by an unusually strong FY2020 (COVID-era inventory destocking + first year of IFRS16 transition creating one-off working-capital tailwinds), while the 3yr figure (26.6%) reflects rebound from the FY2022 trough (post-COVID reopening cost inflation, weak NZ consumer) to a record FY2025. Owner FCF broadly tracks NPAT ($40.7m owner FCF vs $39.5m NPAT in FY2025), confirming the lease-adjusted FCF series is sound; the DCF instead anchors forward growth on revenue/NPBT trends and NZ/AU apparel retail's structurally low-to-mid-single-digit long-run volume growth plus continued Australian expansion.

base.description: Through-cycle growth decelerating from FY2026's strong start (H1 +14.6%) toward a mature ~4% long-run rate; EBIT margin improves modestly from AU scale/Sydney DC efficiencies (13.3% -> 14.5% over 10yr, still below H1-2026's record 15.0%); cash tax rate normalizes toward 29% as AU (30% rate) mix keeps growing; working capital is a modest drag scaling with revenue growth (inventory-heavy retailer, no deferred-revenue tailwind).

bull.description: Glassons Australia rollout + Sydney DC efficiencies sustain high-single/low-double-digit growth for longer; margin expands further (13.8% -> 16.2%) on operating leverage and continued gross-margin discipline; slightly lower tax path (AU tax credits/losses utilisation) and slightly higher terminal growth reflecting durable AU structural growth.

bear.description: NZ/AU consumer recession plus intensifying fast-fashion (Shein/Temu) share loss compress growth to low-single digits and margins fall back toward FY2022-trough levels (12.5% -> 10.9%) as FX/competitive pressure persists without offsetting sourcing gains; working capital drag worsens (inventory write-downs/markdowns in a weak sell-through environment); higher WACC for elevated cyclical/competitive risk.

wacc_rationale: Base WACC 10.5% reflects: NZ risk-free rate ~4.5-5.0%, NZ equity risk premium ~5.5-6.0%, HLG beta modestly above 1.0 given discretionary-retail/consumer-cyclical exposure, small-cap illiquidity premium for a ~NZ$635m market cap NZX stock, plus a ~0.5-1.0pp fashion/cyclical risk premium for unhedged USD sourcing exposure and intensifying online fast-fashion competition (Shein/Temu). No interest-bearing debt (lease liabilities excluded), so WACC ≈ cost of equity. Bull case uses a lower 10.0% WACC (established AU growth track record reduces execution risk); Bear case uses 11.5% (consumer recession + competitive share-loss risk both realized, raising required return).

current_multiples_context.note: Current EV/owner-FCF ~14.2x. Base-case implied exit multiple (12.4x) and bull-case (13.7x) both sit at or below the current multiple, i.e. neither scenario assumes market re-rating/multiple expansion — upside is earned via cash flow growth, not multiple expansion.

entry_price.methodology: PV of Yr1-10 base-case owner FCF at 15% hurdle + PV of Gordon terminal value (computed at WACC, discounted back at 15%) - net debt, all divided by year-10 shares (flat at 59.649m, no dilution).

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC (8.5%-12.5%), Columns = terminal growth (1.25%-3.25%). Values are base-case intrinsic value per share. Cap flattens the top-left corner (low WACC) where Gordon growth would otherwise exceed the 14x terminal-FCF cap.

probability_weighted.weighting_rationale: Base case (50%) reflects the most likely through-cycle outcome given HLG's demonstrated execution (record FY2025, strong H1-2026) tempered by management's own caution that early-season trading is not representative. Bull (25%) reflects continued AU outperformance/margin resilience persisting at current H1-2026 levels. Bear (25%) reflects material risk from NZ/AU consumer softness, unhedged FX, and structural fast-fashion competitive pressure (Shein/Temu) — all explicitly flagged as high-severity risks in the qualitative analysis.

investment_case_notes: HLG is an income-oriented compounder, not a high-growth multi-bagger: ~80-90% earnings payout (FY2025 DPS $0.51 / EPS $0.66), no debt, no buybacks, negligible SBC, flat share count. The DCF/entry-price framework built for growth-reinvestment compounders still applies, but the realistic return profile is dividend yield (~4.8% at current price) plus modest per-share value growth, rather than capital-light reinvestment compounding. Scenarios are framed accordingly: Bull is sustained execution on the known Glassons Australia growth driver, not a step-change business model transformation; Bear is cyclical/competitive margin compression, not existential risk, given the debt-free balance sheet and net cash position ($58.3m FY2025).

data_provenance.lease_principal_repayments_by_year_sourc: Cash flow statement, financing activities, 'Payments for lease liabilities principal' line, HLG.NZ Annual Report FY2020-FY2025 (Extracted/ .txt files), converted from $'000 to $m
data_provenance.tax_rate_note: Effective rate (32.4% FY25, 33.8% FY24) exceeds the 28% NZ statutory rate due to permanent items (non-deductible expenses, prior-period adjustments, one-off building depreciation tax-base removal in FY24). Normalized cash tax rate path uses ~29-31% blending NZ 28%/AU 30% statutory rates as the AU revenue mix (53% FY25) continues to grow, without assuming the effective-rate one-offs recur.

sanity_check.notes: Passed all four trips. Implied P/E 18.4x is above the 10yr FY-end-price average (11.8x) but below the 2x trip bound; HLG is at an all-time-high price with H1-2026 NPBT +32.9%, so a premium to trailing history partly reflects forward earnings. P/B is structurally high for HLG (~90% payout leaves a small book) — 10yr range 3.1-5.5x, so the 6.5x implied P/B on trailing book is a modest premium, not a SEK-style 3.4x-vs-0.99x blowout. EV/EBITDA computed on IFRS16 (post-2019) basis both sides. Multiples use FY-end (August) closes and SBC-adjusted earnings (SBC negligible), so they will not match screener GAAP P/Es.
